I built Crop Atlas to help farmers explore crop options as climate conditions change. Users can search for a place or click on a 3D map, then compare NASA POWER temperature and rainfall data with the conditions different crops need.

The app shows possible climate problems, suggests other crops to explore, and displays available soil estimates. Users can also add crops they grew before to explore what they could grow next and check for shared plant families.

My goal is to bring climate and crop information into one app that is easy to understand. The results are a starting point, not a promise that a crop will grow well. Soil, water supply, planting season, and crop variety still need to be checked.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

I built Crop Atlas to help farmers explore what crops they could grow as climate conditions change due to constant global warming , greenhouse effect and etc.

Users can search for a place or click on the 3D map. The app gets temperature and rainfall data from NASA POWER and compares them with the conditions different crops need. It shows which conditions match and which might be a problem.

Users can also explore other crops, check available soil information, and save crops and places. For crop rotation, they can add crops they grew before and explore options for what to grow next. The app also checks whether crops share the same plant family.

HOW DOES IT HELP?

Crop Atlas puts information from different sources in one app. Users can compare crops and understand the results through simple explanations.

WHAT IS MY GOAL?

I want to make climate and crop information easier for farmers to use. The app can help them find options to look into and discuss with local farming experts.

WHAT DID I USE TO BUILD IT?

I used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code. The website is hosted on GitHub Pages, and I used Canva for the slides.

The data and tools include:

• NASA POWER for temperature and rainfall.

• FAO EcoCrop through OpenCLIM for crop growing conditions.

• ISRIC SoilGrids for soil estimates.

• MapSPAM 2020 for mapped crop-growing areas.

• Google Maps for the 3D map and place search.

AI helped write most of the code, fix errors, and find information.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE?

Users can explore a place on the globe, compare crop options, and check possible next crops in the same app. I wanted it to feel easy to explore instead of making users read through separate data files.

WHAT DID I CONSIDER?

I considered temperature, rainfall, available soil pH, previous crops, and plant families. I also wanted the app to be easy to understand and show when information is missing.

The results do not promise that a crop will grow well. Farmers still need to check their soil, water supply, planting season, and crop variety. Past climate averages are not weather forecasts. A crop being from a different plant family also does not automatically make it a good choice for rotation.
